## Simple explanation

MLOps is the set of practices that helps teams move models from experiments
into reliable production systems and keep them working over time. It combines
machine-learning development with software operations and data management.

## Technical explanation

MLOps covers repeatable workflows for data preparation, training, evaluation,
model and dataset versioning, deployment, monitoring, and retraining. The
extent of automation varies: a small project may use scripts and documented
checks, while a large platform may use orchestration, registries, and
continuous delivery.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Model behavior depends on both code and data, and those can change
independently. MLOps practices make it easier to reproduce a model, trace
which data and configuration produced it, roll out changes safely, and detect
performance or infrastructure problems after deployment.

## How it works

A typical lifecycle automates or standardizes data validation, training,
testing, artifact registration, deployment, and post-deployment monitoring.
The system may trigger a new training run when new data arrives or a monitored
condition requires review. Human approval and rollback mechanisms remain
important safeguards.

## Practical example

A team retrains a demand-forecasting model weekly. Its workflow validates the
new data, trains a candidate, compares it with the current model on a fixed
evaluation set, and only deploys the candidate if it meets release criteria.

## Common misconceptions

- MLOps is not just putting a model behind an API.
- Not every project needs a complex platform; automation should match the project's risk and scale.
- Automated retraining is not automatically beneficial unless candidate models are evaluated before release.
